papers.abstract: The standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown. In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival. In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; P<0.001); estimated overall survival at 24 months was 78.4% and 69.4%, respectively (hazard ratio for death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.83; P = 0.003). Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 60.1% (95% CI, 53.2 to 66.2) with durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (hazard ratio for an event or death vs. control, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71.1% of patients in the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 30.7%), in 79.5% of those in the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 44.5%), and in 50.2% of those in the control group. Perioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups. (Funded by AstraZeneca; VOLGA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04960709; EudraCT number, 2020-005452-38.).

papers.abstract: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

papers.abstract: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. papers.abstract: Abstract Penile squamous cell carcinoma (PeSCC) is a rare malignancy with limited treatment options in advanced stages. The phase II PERICLES trial (NCT03686332) investigated atezolizumab with or without radiotherapy (RT) in advanced penile cancer. Here, we report mature overall survival (OS) and updated progression-free survival (PFS) outcomes and an in-depth biomarker analysis. Patients were treated with atezolizumab monotherapy (n = 12) or atezolizumab in combination with RT (n = 20, 33 fractions of 1.5–1.8 Gy) for locoregional disease control. Comprehensive analysis of baseline tumor tissue (n = 28/31) was performed using bulk RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Additionally, spatial transcriptomics (n = 9) was conducted to further explore functionality and (co-)localization of immune cell subsets. With extended follow-up (median: 38 months), landmark 2-year OS and PFS in the full study cohort was 18.8% [95% confidence interval (CI), 9.1–38.6] and 12.5% (95% CI, 5–31.3), respectively. High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV)-positive tumors were enriched for IFNγ and IFNα signatures, potentially explaining the improved PFS and OS observed in this subgroup. Both stromal CD68+ myeloid cell density and intratumoral CD8+PD-1+ T-cell density were associated with nonprogression at 1 year. Increased intratumoral CD8+PD-1+ T-cell density was also associated with improved PFS and OS, with consistent findings in the hrHPV-positive subgroup. Spatial transcriptomics identified these CD8+ T cells as tissue-resident cytotoxic effector cells coexpressing checkpoint molecules (LAG3 and TIGIT), chemokines (CCL4 and CXCL13), and cytotoxic molecules (PRF1 and GZMB). Interrogation of the penile cancer immune microenvironment highlights CD8+PD-1+ T cells as candidate biomarkers in relation to clinical benefit from immune checkpoint blockade in advanced PeSCC.

papers.abstract: T cell exhaustion within the tumor microenvironment poses a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy, yet the epigenetic mechanisms that preserve functional states of tumor-infiltrating T cells remain incompletely understood. Here, using an in vivo CRISPR screen, we identify heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2/B1 (hnRNPA2B1) as a regulator of CD8+ T cell fitness. Transcriptomic analyses of cancer patient cohorts reveal that hnRNPA2B1 is preferentially enriched in a proliferative, intermediate exhausted T cell subset associated with favorable clinical outcomes. Genetic ablation of hnRNPA2B1 in CD8+ T cells accelerates terminal exhaustion, impairs antitumor immunity, and diminishes responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. Mechanistically, hnRNPA2B1 forms nuclear puncta and stabilizes RNAs involved in chromatin organization, thereby maintaining chromatin accessibility that restrains exhaustion-associated programs while preserving proliferative and cytotoxic potential. Together, these findings establish hnRNPA2B1 as an RNA-mediated epigenetic regulator sustaining functional exhausted T cell states in tumors.

papers.abstract: Scoliosis surgery is complex and associated with significant morbidity. Accurate risk assessment is essential for appropriate resource allocation and improved care. Risk factors for developing complications have been identified; however, structured frameworks to support preoperative assessment are limited. Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) uses a three-tier multidisciplinary team (MDT) traffic-light system to triage patients based on well-defined risk factors and expert clinical judgment. We aimed to describe complications following scoliosis surgery at GOSH and evaluate the relationship between preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment and outcomes such as complication rates, operative times, and length of stay. A retrospective hospital file review was conducted for all patients presenting to GOSH for primary scoliosis surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Institutional approval was obtained, and the need for ethical approval was waived. Preoperative risk is quantified by the MDT using a three-tier traffic-light system categorizing patients as low (green), intermediate (amber), and high-risk (red). Outcomes including 30-day in-hospital complications, operative time, and length of stay were analyzed in relation to preoperative MDT traffic-light score. Of 350 eligible patients, 337 had a documented preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment. Low-risk patients comprised 43.6% (n = 147/337), intermediate-risk 49.3% (n = 166/337), and high-risk 7.1% (n = 24/337). Major complications occurred in 2% (n = 3/147) of low-risk patients compared with 50% (n = 12/24) of high-risk patients, corresponding to an adjusted odds ratio of 11.4 ([95% CI 1.98-65.4], p = 0.006). High-risk patients also had significantly longer operative times (381 min vs. 320 min, p < 0.001) and length of stay (12 days vs. 5 days, p < 0.001) when compared to low-risk patients. Patients classified as high-risk by the MDT demonstrated an increased odds of developing major complications, longer operative time, and extended length of stay when compared to low-risk patients. Similar structured tools, with local adaptations, may be valuable in other centers to support preoperative assessment, shared decision making, and guide resource allocation.

papers.abstract: Hormone receptor positive (HR+) breast cancer is the most common breast cancer subtype globally and remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women. Black women diagnosed HR+ breast cancer experience significantly worse outcomes than White women, a disparity that persists even after accounting for factors such as healthcare access and educational attainment. Understanding the biological mechanisms underlying these differences has been limited by the underrepresentation of Black patients in genomic datasets. To address this gap, we generated an HR+ breast cancer transcriptomic dataset enriched for Black patients while controlling for access to healthcare and education level. Tumors from Black women showed enrichment of tumor microenvironment-related signatures, including increased collagen deposition and prognostically unfavorable T-cell landscapes. Data from in vitro and in vivo experimental models showed that race-aligned collagen deposition patterns were driven, at least in part, by tumor cell-intrinsic signaling and promoted metastatic phenotypes associated with poorer outcomes. Further analysis of the patient transcriptomic dataset revealed that unfavorable T-cell signatures previously attributed to race or ancestry were more strongly associated with poverty burden. Across multiple independent datasets, STAT4 emerged as a potential master regulator of this poverty-associated immune phenotype. Collectively, these findings suggest that molecular features of breast tumors are shaped by both biological and structural factors linked to self-identified race and socioeconomic disadvantage. These results demonstrate that integrating social determinants of health with molecular analyses can reveal mechanisms contributing to cancer outcome disparities and provide a foundation for the development of more effective and equitable precision oncology approaches.

papers.abstract: Patients referred for postoperative care within enhanced care units in the United Kingdom are less likely to have their surgery canceled than those referred to critical care. Presently, it is unclear whether this association remains when examined at an individual hospital level, and whether specific structure and process features of enhanced care services influence cancelation rates within a facility. We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, observational study documenting clinical and organizational features of enhanced and critical care facilities in the United Kingdom. Features of interest included resource protections, staffing, and clinical scope. Sites with availability of both enhanced and critical care facilities, with >10 referrals to enhanced care during the study period, were selected for analysis. Cancelation rates of elective surgery within these facilities were quantified over a 3-month period between September 1, 2023, and November 30, 2023. Rates were defined as the number of elective cases canceled divided by the number of elective referrals to each facility. Multilevel regression was used to explore relationships between structure and process features of enhanced care units and surgical cancelation, using a two-level model with cases nested within hospitals to account for institutional confounding. Complete data were available for 65 sites, of which 28 had an enhanced care facility with sufficient activity for analysis, representing 4112 patients referred to enhanced or critical care. In most institutions, surgical cancelation rates were lower within their enhanced care facility than in critical care. Enhanced care units with beds reserved exclusively for elective cases (odds ratio [OR], 0.54 [0.39-0.76]; P < .001) and clinical care involving multiple specialities (OR, 0.48 [0.33-0.69]; P < .001) were associated with reduced odds of cancelation. On the other hand, enhanced care units that permitted admission of emergency cases (OR, 1.61 [1.06-2.43]; P = .024) were associated with a greater odds of cancelation. Structure and process features of enhanced care pathways are associated with cancelation rates among high-risk surgical patients in the United Kingdom. These findings may explain why cancelation rates in enhanced care are typically lower than within critical care and may have important policy implications.

papers.abstract: Preoperative anxiety affects 30% to 80 % of ambulatory surgery patients and is associated with increased anesthetic requirements, postoperative pain, and delayed recovery. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising nonpharmacological anxiolytic, but evidence remains limited in the ambulatory setting. The AMBLUMEEN (AMBulatory LUMEEN) trial is a single-center, randomized, open-label, superiority trial conducted in an adult ambulatory surgery unit. Patients with moderate-to-severe preoperative anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y-A [STAI-YA] > 45) were randomized 1:1 to standard care alone (control) or standard care and a single 20-minute preoperative VR session (immersive 360° natural contemplative scenes). The primary end point was the change in STAI-YA score from arrival in the ambulatory unit (baseline) to immediately before operating room transfer (presurgery), analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle with a linear mixed model. Secondary end points included preoperative benzodiazepine use, postoperative morphine requirement, unplanned overnight admission, patient satisfaction, and device acceptability. Of 106 randomized patients (53 per group) with a median [interquartile range] baseline STAI-YA of 49 [46-55] and 49 [46-58] respectively in the control and VR group, the VR group experienced a markedly greater reduction in state anxiety than controls. Adjusted mean between-group difference in STAI-YA change from baseline to presurgery was -18.7 95% confidence interval (CI) [-21.4 to -16.1] points in favor of VR. Although benzodiazepine requirement, postoperative pain, and unplanned overnight admission were comparable between groups, the morphine requirement in postanesthesia care unit was lower in the VR group (6/53 [11.3% 95% CI, 11.3 {4.3-23.0}] vs 0/53 [0.0%, 95% CI, {0.0-6.7}]; P = .027). Global perioperative satisfaction was high in both groups (median 8 [8-9] on 10). A single 20-minute session of medical-grade VR significantly reduced preoperative anxiety in ambulatory surgery patients, with high acceptability and an excellent safety profile.

papers.abstract: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear. In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here. A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab. Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer.
